leo: quick thread to lock down iterator+transport handshake. we keep seeing edgecases in retries + pagination across py/ts/go.
ariana: agreed. want to avoid leaking transport primitives (streams vs pages) into the user API. users should get a single "iterate" model.
mike: +1. proposal: a small standardized adapter contract w/ clear error types and a negotiation handshake. adapters implement transport specifics; core implements ergonomics.
leo: sketch of adapter surface: fetch(window, resumeToken, opts) -> {items, resumeToken, cursor_type, transient} ; close(); capabilities()
ariana: i like that. a few open concerns: 1) resume token churn (server rotates) 2) duplicate delivery when reconnecting 3) multiplexed connections (multiple cursors on one conn)
mike: for (1) token versioning: server returns token prefixed w/ version label e.g. "v2:base64". adapters treat it opaque except they should expose version to core for metrics. servers should include "deprecated_until" in response metadata if they're planning rotation.
infra: ops note: when deprecated_until passes, we get many resume_reject events. need a runbook and an automated user-visible banner.
leo: for (2) use idempotency + last-acked-resume per connection. adapter must send X-RW-Req-Id per fetch. server should dedupe by that id. add a small client-side cache: last_successful_resume_by_conn.
ariana: for duplicate-at-least-once semantics some customers are fine; for others we need transactional semantics. hard to guarantee across transports; document clearly.
mike: multiplexing: prefer to ship non-multiplex first. multiplex adds per-cursor flow-control and per-cursor acks. treat as opt-in capability after handshake.
leo: handshake idea: client sends header: "X-RW-Iter-Cap: resume=v2,multiplex=0,alt-resume=1" server responds with supported caps. both sides log capabilities.
ariana: error taxonomy is important. define: TransientError (retryable), ResumeInvalid (must surface/fallback), FatalError (stop). adapters should map transport errors to these types.
mike: example http/json response shape for adapters:
```
{
  "items": [...],
  "resume_token": "v2:BASE64...",
  "cursor_kind": "page|offset|stream-pos",
  "resume_deprecated_until": 1710000000,
  "retryable": true
}
```
leo: core retry policy: window-level backoff by default. if adapter signals ResumeInvalid, core will try alt_resume_hint if present, otherwise surface error to user.
ariana: language ergonomics: py -> (generator / async generator), ts -> AsyncIterable, go -> (chan or Next style). adapters implement the resume token plumbing.
mike: testing: add fuzz tests for malformed tokens, expired tokens, and simulated mid-window reconnects. also test idempotency behavior by replaying the same X-RW-Req-Id.
infra: metrics we need: fetch_latency, fetch_retries, resume_reject_rate, resume_deprecated_alert, multiplex_failures. alerting: resume_reject_rate > 0.5% over 5m for a customer -> pager.
leo: small sample pseudo for core loop (lang-neutral):
```
while it.has_next():
  try:
    batch = adapter.fetch(it.window, it.resume)
  except TransientError:
    backoff_and_retry()
    continue
  if batch.resume_invalid:
    if batch.alt_resume_hint: try_alt(batch.alt_resume_hint)
    else raise ResumeInvalid
  it.emit(batch.items)
  it.update_resume(batch.resume_token)
```
ariana: docs & migration: v1 servers used opaque token no-version. during rollout server may emit both v1 and v2 tokens. adapters accept both. add a compatibility test matrix.
mike: next steps: 1) draft adapter interface PR (leo) 2) prototype python generator + simple http/paged adapter (ariana) 3) go + ts token parsers + tests (mike) 4) ops runbook + alerts (infra)
devx-bot: created RFC draft: https://r.rw/sdks/iter-handshake (automated) :bookmark_tabs:
leo: OK if no objections i'll formalize this as a short RFC. :thumbsup:
